1.s:
śrī devy uvāca |
śrutaṃ deva mayā sarvaṃ rudrayāmalasambhavam |
trikabhedam aśeṣeṇa sārāt sāravibhāgaśaḥ || 1 ||
1.d:
श्री देव्य् उवाच ।
श्रुतं देव मया सर्वं रुद्रयामलसम्भवम् ।
त्रिकभेदम् अशेषेण सारात् सारविभागशः ॥ 1 ॥
1.m:
The venerable Goddess said:
I have heard, O God, all that arises from the Rudrayāmala, / [including] the division of the Trika entirely, broken down into the essence of essences.

2.s:
adyāpi na nivṛtto me saṃśayaḥ parameśvara |
kiṃ rūpaṃ tattvato deva śabdarāśikalāmayam || 2 ||
2.d:
अद्यापि न निवृत्तो मे संशयः परमेश्वर ।
किं रूपं तत्त्वतो देव शब्दराशिकलामयम् ॥ 2 ॥
2.m: Even now, O Supreme Lord, my doubt has not ceased: / O God, what is in truth [Bhairava’s] nature? Does it consist of the collection of sounds and its phonemic powers? || 2

3.s:
kiṃ vā navātmabhedena bhairave bhairavākṛtau |
triśirobhedabhinnaṃ vā kiṃ vā śaktitrayātmakam || 3 ||
3.d:
किं वा नवात्मभेदेन भैरवे भैरवाकृतौ ।
त्रिशिरोभेदभिन्नं वा किं वा शक्तित्रयात्मकम् ॥ 3 ॥
3.m: Or is Bhairava of the nature of the division of Navātman? / Or is he differentiated according to the division of Triśiras? Or does he consist of the triad of Śaktis? || 3

4.s:
nādabindumayaṃ vāpi kiṃ candrārdhanirodhikāḥ |
cakrārūḍham anackaṃ vā kiṃ vā śaktisvarūpakam || 4 ||
4.d:
नादबिन्दुमयं वापि किं चन्द्रार्धनिरोधिकाः ।
चक्रारूढम् अनच्कं वा किं वा शक्तिस्वरूपकम् ॥ 4 ॥
4.m: Or does it consist of subtle sonic resonance and the point of concentrated energy? Or is it the half-moon and the obstructress? / Or is it mounted on the energy centers, devoid of vowels, or of the intrinsic nature of Śakti? || 4

5.s:
parāparāyāḥ sakalam aparāyāś ca vā punaḥ |
parāyā yadi tadvat syāt paratvaṃ tad virudhyate || 5 ||
5.d:
परापरायाः सकलम् अपरायाश् च वा पुनः ।
पराया यदि तद्वत् स्यात् परत्वं तद् विरुध्यते ॥ 5 ॥
5.m: Is it manifest with parts in the case of the Supreme-cum-Non-Supreme, or again of the Non-Supreme? / If it were likewise in the case of the Supreme, then its supremacy would be contradicted. || 5

6.s:
na hi varṇavibhedena dehabhedena vā bhavet |
paratvaṃ niṣkalatvena sakalatve na tad bhavet || 6 ||
6.d:
न हि वर्णविभेदेन देहभेदेन वा भवेत् ।
परत्वं निष्कलत्वेन सकलत्वे न तद् भवेत् ॥ 6 ॥
6.m: For supremacy cannot consist in differentiation of phonemes or bodies; / it consists in being transcendent without parts, not in being manifest with parts. || 6

7.s:
prasādaṃ kuru me nātha niḥśeṣaṃ chinddhi saṃśayam |
bhairava uvāca |
sādhu sādhu tvayā pṛṣṭaṃ tantrasāram idam priye || 7 ||
7.d:
प्रसादं कुरु मे नाथ निःशेषं छिन्द्धि संशयम् ।
भैरव उवाच ।
साधु साधु त्वया पृष्टं तन्त्रसारम् इदम् प्रिये ॥ 7 ॥
7.m:
Grant me favor, O Lord! Sever my doubt completely!
Bhairava said:
Well asked, well asked, O beloved! This is the essence of the tantras.

8.s:
gūhanīyatamam bhadre tathāpi kathayāmi te |
yatkiṃcit sakalaṃ rūpaṃ bhairavasya prakīrtitam || 8 ||
8.d:
गूहनीयतमम् भद्रे तथापि कथयामि ते ।
यत्किंचित् सकलं रूपं भैरवस्य प्रकीर्तितम् ॥ 8 ॥
8.m: Although it is the most secret of secrets, O auspicious one, I will tell it to you: / Whatever form of Bhairava has been proclaimed as manifest with parts, || 8

9.s:
tad asāratayā devi vijñeyaṃ śakrajālavat |
māyāsvapnopamaṃ caiva gandharvanagarabhramam || 9 ||
9.d:
तद् असारतया देवि विज्ञेयं शक्रजालवत् ।
मायास्वप्नोपमं चैव गन्धर्वनगरभ्रमम् ॥ 9 ॥
9.m: that, O goddess, should be known to be devoid of essence, like Indra's net [of illusion], / like cosmic illusion and dreams, and an illusion of a celestial city in the clouds. || 9

10.s:
dhyānārtham bhrāntabuddhīnāṃ kriyāḍambaravartinām |
kevalaṃ varṇitam puṃsāṃ vikalpanihatātmanām || 10 ||
10.d:
ध्यानार्थम् भ्रान्तबुद्धीनां क्रियाडम्बरवर्तिनाम् ।
केवलं वर्णितम् पुंसां विकल्पनिहतात्मनाम् ॥ 10 ॥
10.m: It was described solely for the meditation of those whose intellects are deluded, / who engage in the ostentation of ritual acts, whose self is crushed by conceptual constructions. || 10

11.s:
tattvato na navātmāsau śabdarāśir na bhairavaḥ |
na cāsau triśirā devo na ca śaktitrayātmakaḥ || 11 ||
11.d:
तत्त्वतो न नवात्मासौ शब्दराशिर् न भैरवः ।
न चासौ त्रिशिरा देवो न च शक्तित्रयात्मकः ॥ 11 ॥
11.m: In ultimate truth, Bhairava is not Navātman, nor is he the collection of sounds; / nor is he the three-headed god Triśiras, nor does he consist of the triad of Śaktis. || 11

12.s:
nādabindumayo vāpi na candrārdhanirodhikāḥ |
na cakrakramasambhinno na ca śaktisvarūpakaḥ || 12 ||
12.d:
नादबिन्दुमयो वापि न चन्द्रार्धनिरोधिकाः ।
न चक्रक्रमसम्भिन्नो न च शक्तिस्वरूपकः ॥ 12 ॥
12.m: Nor does he consist of subtle sonic resonance and the point of concentrated energy, nor the half-moon and the obstructress; / nor is he dissected by the progression of energy centers, nor is he merely of the intrinsic nature of Śakti. || 12

13.s:
aprabuddhamatīnāṃ hi etā balavibhīṣikāḥ |
mātṛmodakavat sarvaṃ pravṛttyarthaṃ udāhṛtam || 13 ||
13.d:
अप्रबुद्धमतीनां हि एता बलविभीषिकाः ।
मातृमोदकवत् सर्वं प्रवृत्त्यर्थं उदाहृतम् ॥ 13 ॥
13.m: For these are terrifying bugbears to frighten children, intended for those of unawakened intellect; / it is all taught like a mother's sweetmeat to induce engagement. || 13

14.s:
dikkālakalanonmuktā deśoddeśāviśeṣinī |
vyapadeṣṭum aśakyāsāv akathyā paramārthataḥ || 14 ||
14.d:
दिक्कालकलनोन्मुक्ता देशोद्देशाविशेषिनी ।
व्यपदेष्टुम् अशक्यासाव् अकथ्या परमार्थतः ॥ 14 ॥
14.m: Free from reckoning by space and time, unqualified by spatial location, / it is impossible to designate, inexpressible in ultimate truth. || 14

15.s:
antaḥsvānubhavānandā vikalponmuktagocarā |
yāvasthā bharitākārā bhairavī bhairavātmanaḥ || 15 ||
15.d:
अन्तःस्वानुभवानन्दा विकल्पोन्मुक्तगोचरा ।
यावस्था भरिताकारा भैरवी भैरवात्मनः ॥ 15 ॥
15.m: Having the bliss of inner direct self-experience, an object accessible only when freed from conceptual construction— / that state which is full in nature of the self that is Bhairava, O Bhairavī, || 15

16.s:
tad vapus tattvato jñeyaṃ vimalaṃ viśvapūraṇam |
evaṃvidhe pare tattve kaḥ pūjyaḥ kaś ca tṛpyati || 16 ||
16.d:
तद् वपुस् तत्त्वतो ज्ञेयं विमलं विश्वपूरणम् ।
एवंविधे परे तत्त्वे कः पूज्यः कश् च तृप्यति ॥ 16 ॥
16.m: that form is in truth to be known as stainless and filling the universe. / In such a supreme reality, who is to be worshipped, and who is satisfied? || 16

17.s:
evaṃvidhā bhairavasya yāvasthā parigīyate |
sā parā pararūpeṇa parā devī prakīrtitā || 17 ||
17.d:
एवंविधा भैरवस्य यावस्था परिगीयते ।
सा परा पररूपेण परा देवी प्रकीर्तिता ॥ 17 ॥
17.m: Such a state of Bhairava as is proclaimed, / that, in the highest sense, is celebrated as the Supreme Goddess. || 17

18.s:
śaktiśaktimator yadvad abhedaḥ sarvadā sthitaḥ |
atas taddharmadharmitvāt parā śaktiḥ parātmanaḥ || 18 ||
18.d:
शक्तिशक्तिमतोर् यद्वद् अभेदः सर्वदा स्थितः ।
अतस् तद्धर्मधर्मित्वात् परा शक्तिः परात्मनः ॥ 18 ॥
18.m: Just as there is always non-differentiation between power and the possessor of power, / therefore, because she shares the attribute and the possessor of the attribute, the Supreme Śakti belongs to the Supreme Self. || 18

19.s:
na vahner dāhikā śaktir vyatiriktā vibhāvyate |
kevalaṃ jñānasattāyām prārambho 'yam praveśane || 19 ||
19.d:
न वह्नेर् दाहिका शक्तिर् व्यतिरिक्ता विभाव्यते ।
केवलं ज्ञानसत्तायाम् प्रारम्भो ऽयम् प्रवेशने ॥ 19 ॥
19.m: The burning power of fire is not conceived as distinct [from the fire itself]; / this [distinction] is merely an initiation into entry into the reality of knowledge. || 19

20.s:
śaktyavasthāpraviṣṭasya nirvibhāgena bhāvanā |
tadāsau śivarūpī syāt śaivī mukham ihocyate || 20 ||
20.d:
शक्त्यवस्थाप्रविष्टस्य निर्विभागेन भावना ।
तदासौ शिवरूपी स्यात् शैवी मुखम् इहोच्यते ॥ 20 ॥
20.m: For one who has entered the state of Śakti, there is contemplative realization without differentiation; / then that one assumes the nature of Śiva. The Śākta [power] is declared here to be the face [of entrance]. || 20

21.s:
yathālokena dīpasya kiraṇair bhāskarasya ca |
jñāyate digvibhāgādi tadvac chaktyā śivaḥ priye || 21 ||
21.d:
यथालोकेन दीपस्य किरणैर् भास्करस्य च ।
ज्ञायते दिग्विभागादि तद्वच् छक्त्या शिवः प्रिये ॥ 21 ॥
21.m: Just as directions and the like are known by the illumination of a lamp or the rays of the sun, / so too, O beloved, is Śiva [known] by means of Śakti. || 21

22.s:
śrī devy uvāca |
devadeva triśūlāṅka kapālakṛtabhūṣaṇa |
digdeśakālaśūnyā ca vyapadeśavivarjitā || 22 ||
22.d:
श्री देव्य् उवाच ।
देवदेव त्रिशूलाङ्क कपालकृतभूषण ।
दिग्देशकालशून्या च व्यपदेशविवर्जिता ॥ 22 ॥
22.m:
The venerable Goddess said:
O God of gods, adorned with a skull, bearing the mark of the trident,
[she who is] devoid of direction, space, and time, and free of any designation,

23.s:
yāvasthā bharitākārā bhairavasyopalabhyate |
kair upāyair mukhaṃ tasya parā devi katham bhavet |
yathā samyag ahaṃ vedmi tathā me brūhi bhairava || 23 ||
23.d:
यावस्था भरिताकारा भैरवस्योपलभ्यते ।
कैर् उपायैर् मुखं तस्य परा देवि कथम् भवेत् ।
यथा सम्यग् अहं वेद्मि तथा मे ब्रूहि भैरव ॥ 23 ॥
23.m: that state of Bhairava which is realized to be full in nature: / By what contemplative means may the Supreme Goddess become his face? / Tell me, O Bhairava, so that I may comprehend it completely! || 23

24.s:
bhairava uvāca |
ūrdhve prāṇo hy adho jīvo visargātmā paroccaret |
utpattidvitayasthāne bharaṇād bharitā sthitiḥ || 24 ||
24.d:
भैरव उवाच ।
ऊर्ध्वे प्राणो ह्य् अधो जीवो विसर्गात्मा परोच्चरेत् ।
उत्पत्तिद्वितयस्थाने भरणाद् भरिता स्थितिः ॥ 24 ॥
24.m:
Bhairava said:
Upward rises the exhalation, and downward the inhalation; the Supreme [Goddess] whose nature is emission rises up. / By filling the two places of origination, the state of plenitude [arises].

25.s:
maruto 'ntar bahir vāpi viyadyugmānivartanāt |
bhairavyā bhairavasyettham bhairavi vyajyate vapuḥ || 25 ||
25.d:
मरुतो ऽन्तर् बहिर् वापि वियद्युग्मानिवर्तनात् ।
भैरव्या भैरवस्येत्थम् भैरवि व्यज्यते वपुः ॥ 25 ॥
25.m: Whether the breath is internal or external, by stopping the pair of spaces, / through Bhairavī the form of Bhairava is thus revealed, O Bhairavī! || 25

26.s:
na vrajen na viśec chaktir marudrūpā vikāsite |
nirvikalpatayā madhye tayā bhairavarūpatā || 26 ||
26.d:
न व्रजेन् न विशेच् छक्तिर् मरुद्रूपा विकासिते ।
निर्विकल्पतया मध्ये तया भैरवरूपता ॥ 26 ॥
26.m: When [the center] has unfolded, let the power in the form of breath neither go out nor enter; / by means of that [power], free from conceptual construction in the center, the nature of Bhairava [is attained]. || 26

27.s:
kumbhitā recitā vāpi pūritā vā yadā bhavet |
tadante śāntanāmāsau śaktyā śāntaḥ prakāśate || 27 ||
27.d:
कुम्भिता रेचिता वापि पूरिता वा यदा भवेत् ।
तदन्ते शान्तनामासौ शक्त्या शान्तः प्रकाशते ॥ 27 ॥
27.m: When it is retained, exhaled, or inhaled, / at the end of that, the quiescent state shines forth through the power named the quiescent. || 27

28.s:
āmūlāt kiraṇābhāsāṃ sūkṣmāt sūkṣmatarātmikam |
cintayet tāṃ dviṣaṭkānte śyāmyantīm bhairavodayaḥ || 28 ||
28.d:
आमूलात् किरणाभासां सूक्ष्मात् सूक्ष्मतरात्मिकम् ।
चिन्तयेत् तां द्विषट्कान्ते श्याम्यन्तीम् भैरवोदयः ॥ 28 ॥
28.m: One should contemplate that [power] having the brilliance of rays from the root, subtler than the subtlest, / dissolving at the end of the twelve; [then] the dawn of Bhairava [occurs]. || 28

29.s:
udgacchantīṃ taḍitrūpām praticakraṃ kramāt kramam |
ūrdhvaṃ muṣṭitrayaṃ yāvat tāvad ante mahodayaḥ || 29 ||
29.d:
उद्गच्छन्तीं तडित्रूपाम् प्रतिचक्रं क्रमात् क्रमम् ।
ऊर्ध्वं मुष्टित्रयं यावत् तावद् अन्ते महोदयः ॥ 29 ॥
29.m: Rising up in the form of lightning, energy center by energy center, in succession, / up to three spans above [the crown]; then at the end, the great dawn [occurs]. || 29

30.s:
kramadvādaśakaṃ samyag dvādaśākṣarabheditam |
sthūlasūkṣmaparasthityā muktvā muktvāntataḥ śivaḥ || 30 ||
30.d:
क्रमद्वादशकं सम्यग् द्वादशाक्षरभेदितम् ।
स्थूलसूक्ष्मपरस्थित्या मुक्त्वा मुक्त्वान्ततः शिवः ॥ 30 ॥
30.m: The twelvefold progression, properly differentiated by the twelve syllables, / releasing each in turn through the coarse, subtle, and supreme states—at the end, Śiva [arises]. || 30

31.s:
tayāpūryāśu mūrdhāntaṃ bhaṅktvā bhrūkṣepasetunā |
nirvikalpaṃ manaḥ kṛtvā sarvordhve sarvagodgamaḥ || 31 ||
31.d:
तयापूर्याशु मूर्धान्तं भङ्क्त्वा भ्रूक्षेपसेतुना ।
निर्विकल्पं मनः कृत्वा सर्वोर्ध्वे सर्वगोद्गमः ॥ 31 ॥
31.m: Filling quickly with that [power] up to the crown, having broken through the bridge of the brow-gesture, / and making the mind free from conceptual construction, the all-pervading rises at the supreme summit. || 31

32.s:
śikhipakṣaiś citrarūpair maṇḍalaiḥ śūnyapañcakam |
dhyāyato 'nuttare śūnye praveśo hṛdaye bhavet || 32 ||
32.d:
शिखिपक्षैश् चित्ररूपैर् मण्डलैः शून्यपञ्चकम् ।
ध्यायतो ऽनुत्तरे शून्ये प्रवेशो हृदये भवेत् ॥ 32 ॥
32.m: Meditating on the five voids as circles variegated like peacock feathers, / an entry into the unexcelled void in the heart occurs.

33.s:
īdṛśena krameṇaiva yatra kutrāpi cintanā |
śūnye kuḍye pare pātre svayaṃ līnā varapradā || 33 ||
33.d:
ईदृशेन क्रमेणैव यत्र कुत्रापि चिन्तना ।
शून्ये कुड्ये परे पात्रे स्वयं लीना वरप्रदा ॥ 33 ॥
33.m: In this very manner, wherever contemplative thought is directed— / in the void, on a wall, or on an excellent disciple—it dissolves of itself and grants the boon. || 33

34.s:
kapālāntar mano nyasya tiṣṭhan mīlitalocanaḥ |
krameṇa manaso dārḍhyāt lakṣayet laṣyam uttamam || 34 ||
34.d:
कपालान्तर् मनो न्यस्य तिष्ठन् मीलितलोचनः ।
क्रमेण मनसो दार्ढ्यात् लक्षयेत् लष्यम् उत्तमम् ॥ 34 ॥
34.m: Placing the mind inside the skull, remaining with closed eyes, / through the gradual firmness of the mind, one should perceive the supreme target. || 34

35.s:
madhyanāḍī madhyasaṃsthā bisasūtrābharūpayā |
dhyātāntarvyomayā devyā tayā devaḥ prakāśate || 35 ||
35.d:
मध्यनाडी मध्यसंस्था बिससूत्राभरूपया ।
ध्यातान्तर्व्योमया देव्या तया देवः प्रकाशते ॥ 35 ॥
35.m: The central channel is situated in the middle, resembling a lotus-fiber thread; / contemplated as the inner space by means of the goddess, through her the God shines forth. || 35

36.s:
kararuddhadṛgastreṇa bhrūbhedād dvārarodhanāt |
dṛṣṭe bindau kramāl līne tanmadhye paramā sthitiḥ || 36 ||
36.d:
कररुद्धदृगस्त्रेण भ्रूभेदाद् द्वाररोधनात् ।
दृष्टे बिन्दौ क्रमाल् लीने तन्मध्ये परमा स्थितिः ॥ 36 ॥
36.m: With the hands blocking the eyes like a weapon, through the piercing of the brows and obstruction of the doors, / when the point of concentrated energy is seen and gradually dissolved, the supreme state is in the midst of it. || 36

37.s:
dhāmāntaḥkṣobhasambhūtasūkṣmāgnitilakākṛtim |
binduṃ śikhānte hṛdaye layānte dhyāyato layaḥ || 37 ||
37.d:
धामान्तःक्षोभसम्भूतसूक्ष्माग्नितिलकाकृतिम् ।
बिन्दुं शिखान्ते हृदये लयान्ते ध्यायतो लयः ॥ 37 ॥
37.m: Meditating on the point of concentrated energy in the shape of a subtle mark of fire, produced by agitation within the seat [of the heart], / at the end of the crest and in the heart, dissolution occurs for the meditator at the end of absorption. || 37

38.s:
anāhate pātrakarṇe 'bhagnaśabde sariddrute |
śabdabrahmaṇi niṣṇātaḥ param brahmādhigacchati || 38 ||
38.d:
अनाहते पात्रकर्णे ऽभग्नशब्दे सरिद्द्रुते ।
शब्दब्रह्मणि निष्णातः परम् ब्रह्माधिगच्छति ॥ 38 ॥
38.m: Immersed in the unstruck sound, entering the ear like an uninterrupted rushing river, / in the Sonic Absolute, one attains the Supreme Absolute. || 38

39.s:
praṇavādisamuccārāt plutānte śūnyabhāvānāt |
śūnyayā parayā śaktyā śūnyatām eti bhairavi || 39 ||
39.d:
प्रणवादिसमुच्चारात् प्लुतान्ते शून्यभावानात् ।
शून्यया परया शक्त्या शून्यताम् एति भैरवि ॥ 39 ॥
39.m: From the sound of the syllable Om and the like, through contemplative realization of the void at the end of the protracted sound, / by means of the supreme power of the void, one attains the state of void, O Bhairavī! || 39

40.s:
yasya kasyāpi varṇasya pūrvāntāv anubhāvayet |
śūnyayā śūnyabhūto 'sau śūnyākāraḥ pumān bhavet || 40 ||
40.d:
यस्य कस्यापि वर्णस्य पूर्वान्ताव् अनुभावयेत् ।
शून्यया शून्यभूतो ऽसौ शून्याकारः पुमान् भवेत् ॥ 40 ॥
40.m: One should experience the beginning and the end of any syllable whatsoever; / having become void through that void [power], a person assumes the nature of the void. || 40

41.s:
tantryādivādyaśabdeṣu dīrgheṣu kramasaṃsthiteḥ |
ananyacetāḥ pratyante paravyomavapur bhavet || 41 ||
41.d:
तन्त्र्यादिवाद्यशब्देषु दीर्घेषु क्रमसंस्थितेः ।
अनन्यचेताः प्रत्यन्ते परव्योमवपुर् भवेत् ॥ 41 ॥
41.m: When sounds of musical instruments such as stringed lutes are elongated and properly arranged in sequence, / one whose mind is undivided becomes at the very end of the form of supreme ether. || 41

42.s:
piṇḍamantrasya sarvasya sthūlavarṇakrameṇa tu |
ardhendubindunādāntaḥ śūnyoccārād bhavec chivaḥ || 42 ||
42.d:
पिण्डमन्त्रस्य सर्वस्य स्थूलवर्णक्रमेण तु ।
अर्धेन्दुबिन्दुनादान्तः शून्योच्चाराद् भवेच् छिवः ॥ 42 ॥
42.m: Of an entire composite mantra, through the sequence of gross phonemes, / ending in the half-moon, point of concentrated energy, and subtle sonic resonance, by voicing into the void one becomes Śiva.

43.s:
nijadehe sarvadikkaṃ yugapad bhāvayed viyat |
nirvikalpamanās tasya viyat sarvam pravartate || 43 ||
43.d:
निजदेहे सर्वदिक्कं युगपद् भावयेद् वियत् ।
निर्विकल्पमनास् तस्य वियत् सर्वम् प्रवर्तते ॥ 43 ॥
43.m: One should contemplate space in one’s own body simultaneously in every direction; / for one whose mind is free from conceptual construction, everything unfolds as ether. || 43

44.s:
pṛṣṭaśūnyaṃ mūlaśūnyaṃ yugapad bhāvayec ca yaḥ |
śarīranirapekṣiṇyā śaktyā śūnyamanā bhavet || 44 ||
44.d:
पृष्टशून्यं मूलशून्यं युगपद् भावयेच् च यः ।
शरीरनिरपेक्षिण्या शक्त्या शून्यमना भवेत् ॥ 44 ॥
44.m:
And whoever contemplates simultaneously the void behind and the void at the root,
through the energy that is independent of the body, becomes of void mind. || 44

45.s:
pṛṣṭaśūnyaṃ mūlaśūnyaṃ hṛcchūnyam bhāvayet sthiram |
yugapan nirvikalpatvān nirvikalpodayas tataḥ || 45 ||
45.d:
पृष्टशून्यं मूलशून्यं हृच्छून्यम् भावयेत् स्थिरम् ।
युगपन् निर्विकल्पत्वान् निर्विकल्पोदयस् ततः ॥ 45 ॥
45.m:
One should contemplate steadily the void behind, the void at the root, and the void of the heart;
simultaneously, because of freedom from conceptual construction, the state free from conceptual construction arises therefrom. || 45

46.s:
tanūdeśe śūnyataiva kṣaṇamātraṃ vibhāvayet |
nirvikalpaṃ nirvikalpo nirvikalpasvarūpabhāk || 46 ||
46.d:
तनूदेशे शून्यतैव क्षणमात्रं विभावयेत् ।
निर्विकल्पं निर्विकल्पो निर्विकल्पस्वरूपभाक् ॥ 46 ॥
46.m:
One should contemplate mere voidness in a region of the body for only a moment,
free from conceptual construction; [thus] free from conceptual construction, one partakes of the nature that is free from conceptual construction. || 46

47.s:
sarvaṃ dehagataṃ dravyaṃ viyadvyāptaṃ mṛgekṣaṇe |
vibhāvayet tatas tasya bhāvanā sā sthirā bhavet || 47 ||
47.d:
सर्वं देहगतं द्रव्यं वियद्व्याप्तं मृगेक्षणे ।
विभावयेत् ततस् तस्य भावना सा स्थिरा भवेत् ॥ 47 ॥
47.m:
O gazelle-eyed one, one should contemplate all substance residing in the body
as pervaded by ether; then that contemplative realization of his becomes firm. || 47

48.s:
dehāntare tvagvibhāgam bhittibhūtaṃ vicintayet |
na kiṃcid antare tasya dhyāyann adhyeyabhāg bhavet || 48 ||
48.d:
देहान्तरे त्वग्विभागम् भित्तिभूतं विचिन्तयेत् ।
न किंचिद् अन्तरे तस्य ध्यायन्न् अध्येयभाग् भवेत् ॥ 48 ॥
48.m:
Inside the body, one should contemplate the partition of the skin as a wall;
meditating that there is nothing inside it, one comes to share in what cannot be meditated upon. || 48

49.s:
hṛdyākāśe nilīnākṣaḥ padmasampuṭamadhyagaḥ |
ananyacetāḥ subhage paraṃ saubhāgyam āpnuyāt || 49 ||
49.d:
हृद्याकाशे निलीनाक्षः पद्मसम्पुटमध्यगः ।
अनन्यचेताः सुभगे परं सौभाग्यम् आप्नुयात् ॥ 49 ॥
49.m:
With senses merged in the space of the heart, entering into the center of the lotus vessel,
with no other thought in mind, O fortunate lady, one attains the supreme fortune. || 49

50.s:
sarvataḥ svaśarīrasya dvādaśānte manolayāt |
dṛḍhabuddher dṛḍhībhūtaṃ tattvalakṣyam pravartate || 50 ||
50.d:
सर्वतः स्वशरीरस्य द्वादशान्ते मनोलयात् ।
दृढबुद्धेर् दृढीभूतं तत्त्वलक्ष्यम् प्रवर्तते ॥ 50 ॥
50.m:
From the dissolution of the mind everywhere in one's body at the end of the twelve,
for one whose intellect is firm, the steady focus on reality unfolds. || 50

51.s:
yathā tathā yatra tatra dvādaśānte manaḥ kṣipet ||
pratikṣaṇaṃ kṣīṇavṛtter vailakṣaṇyaṃ dinair bhavet || 51 ||
51.d:
यथा तथा यत्र तत्र द्वादशान्ते मनः क्षिपेत् ॥
प्रतिक्षणं क्षीणवृत्तेर् वैलक्षण्यं दिनैर् भवेत् ॥ 51 ॥
51.m: In whatever way, wherever, one should cast the mind into the end of the twelve. / For one whose mental fluctuations diminish moment by moment, an extraordinary state emerges in days.

52.s:
kālāgninā kālapadād utthitena svakam puram |
pluṣṭam vicintayed ante śāntābhāsas tadā bhavet || 52 ||
52.d:
कालाग्निना कालपदाद् उत्थितेन स्वकम् पुरम् ।
प्लुष्टम् विचिन्तयेद् अन्ते शान्ताभासस् तदा भवेत् ॥ 52 ॥
52.m:
One should contemplate one's own city burnt by the fire of time
arisen from the plane of time; in the end, one then becomes one whose light is quiescent. || 52

53.s:
evam eva jagat sarvaṃ dagdhaṃ dhyātvā vikalpataḥ |
ananyacetasaḥ puṃsaḥ pumbhāvaḥ paramo bhavet || 53 ||
53.d:
एवम् एव जगत् सर्वं दग्धं ध्यात्वा विकल्पतः ।
अनन्यचेतसः पुंसः पुम्भावः परमो भवेत् ॥ 53 ॥
53.m:
Just so, having meditated conceptually that the whole universe is burnt,
for a person of single-minded focus, the supreme state of the Self arises. || 53

54.s:
svadehe jagato vāpi sūkṣmasūkṣmatarāṇi ca |
tattvāni yāni nilayaṃ dhyātvānte vyajyate parā || 54 ||
54.d:
स्वदेहे जगतो वापि सूक्ष्मसूक्ष्मतराणि च ।
तत्त्वानि यानि निलयं ध्यात्वान्ते व्यज्यते परा ॥ 54 ॥
54.m:
Having meditated upon the dissolution of whatever realities are subtle and subtler
in one's own body or in the universe, in the end the Supreme [Goddess] is revealed. || 54

55.s:
pināṃ ca durbalāṃ śaktiṃ dhyātvā dvādaśagocare |
praviśya hṛdaye dhyāyan muktaḥ svātantryam āpnuyāt || 55 ||
55.d:
पिनां च दुर्बलां शक्तिं ध्यात्वा द्वादशगोचरे ।
प्रविश्य हृदये ध्यायन् मुक्तः स्वातन्त्र्यम् आप्नुयात् ॥ 55 ॥
55.m:
Having meditated upon the gross and feeble energy in the domain of the twelve,
and having entered into the heart while meditating, liberated, one attains autonomy. || 55

56.s:
bhuvanādhvādirūpeṇa cintayet kramaśo 'khilam |
sthūlasūkṣmaparasthityā yāvad ante manolayaḥ || 56 ||
56.d:
भुवनाध्वादिरूपेण चिन्तयेत् क्रमशो ऽखिलम् ।
स्थूलसूक्ष्मपरस्थित्या यावद् अन्ते मनोलयः ॥ 56 ॥
56.m:
One should contemplate everything gradually in the form of the path of the worlds and so forth,
through the gross, subtle, and supreme states, until in the end the mind dissolves. || 56

57.s:
asya sarvasya viśvasya paryanteṣu samantataḥ |
adhvaprakriyayā tattvaṃ śaivaṃ dhyatvā mahodayaḥ || 57 ||
57.d:
अस्य सर्वस्य विश्वस्य पर्यन्तेषु समन्ततः ।
अध्वप्रक्रियया तत्त्वं शैवं ध्यत्वा महोदयः ॥ 57 ॥
57.m:
At the limits of this entire universe in all directions,
having meditated through the procedure of the paths upon the reality of Śiva, great awakening ensues. || 57

58.s:
viśvam etan mahādevi śūnyabhūtaṃ vicintayet |
tatraiva ca mano līnaṃ tatas tallayabhājanam || 58 ||
58.d:
विश्वम् एतन् महादेवि शून्यभूतं विचिन्तयेत् ।
तत्रैव च मनो लीनं ततस् तल्लयभाजनम् ॥ 58 ॥
58.m:
O Great Goddess, one should contemplate this universe as become void;
and there itself the mind is dissolved; thence one is receptive to dissolution therein. || 58

59.s:
ghatādibhājane dṛṣṭim bhittis tyaktvā vinikṣipet |
tallayaṃ tatkṣaṇād gatvā tallayāt tanmayo bhavet || 59 ||
59.d:
घतादिभाजने दृष्टिम् भित्तिस् त्यक्त्वा विनिक्षिपेत् ।
तल्लयं तत्क्षणाद् गत्वा तल्लयात् तन्मयो भवेत् ॥ 59 ॥
59.m:
Having disregarded the wall, one should cast one's gaze into a vessel such as a jar;
going instantly into dissolution therein, one becomes identified with it through that dissolution. || 59

60.s:
nirvṛkṣagiribhittyādideśe dṛṣṭiṃ vinikṣipet |
vilīne mānase bhāve vṛttikṣiṇaḥ prajāyate || 60 ||
60.d:
निर्वृक्षगिरिभित्त्यादिदेशे दृष्टिं विनिक्षिपेत् ।
विलीने मानसे भावे वृत्तिक्षिणः प्रजायते ॥ 60 ॥
60.m:
One should cast one's gaze upon a place devoid of trees, mountains, walls, and the like;
when the mental state is dissolved, one becomes one whose mental fluctuations have ceased. || 60

61.s:
ubhayor bhāvayor jñāne dhyātvā madhyaṃ samāśrayet |
yugapac ca dvayaṃ tyaktvā madhye tattvam prakāśate || 61 ||
61.d:
उभयोर् भावयोर् ज्ञाने ध्यात्वा मध्यं समाश्रयेत् ।
युगपच् च द्वयं त्यक्त्वा मध्ये तत्त्वम् प्रकाशते ॥ 61 ॥
61.m:
In the perception of two objects, having meditated, one should take refuge in the center;
and having abandoned both simultaneously, reality shines forth in the center. || 61

62.s:
bhāve tyakte niruddhā cin naiva bhāvāntaraṃ vrajet |
tadā tanmadhyabhāvena vikasatyati bhāvanā || 62 ||
62.d:
भावे त्यक्ते निरुद्धा चिन् नैव भावान्तरं व्रजेत् ।
तदा तन्मध्यभावेन विकसत्यति भावना ॥ 62 ॥
62.m:
When an object has been abandoned, consciousness held back does not move toward another object;
then through the state between the two, contemplative realization unfolds intensely. || 62

63.s:
sarvaṃ dehaṃ cinmayaṃ hi jagad vā paribhāvayet |
yugapan nirvikalpena manasā paramodayaḥ || 63 ||
63.d:
सर्वं देहं चिन्मयं हि जगद् वा परिभावयेत् ।
युगपन् निर्विकल्पेन मनसा परमोदयः ॥ 63 ॥
63.m:
One should contemplate the whole body or the universe as composed of consciousness;
simultaneously, with a mind free from conceptual construction, the supreme awakening occurs. || 63

64.s:
vāyudvayasya saṃghaṭṭād antar vā bahir antataḥ |
yogī samatvavijñānasamudgamanabhājanam || 64 ||
64.d:
वायुद्वयस्य संघट्टाद् अन्तर् वा बहिर् अन्ततः ।
योगी समत्वविज्ञानसमुद्गमनभाजनम् ॥ 64 ॥
64.m:
From the collision of the two breaths inside or outside at the end,
the yogin becomes a vessel for the emergence of the realization of equanimity. || 64

65.s:
sarvaṃ jagat svadehaṃ vā svānandabharitaṃ smaret |
yugapat svāmṛtenaiva parānandamayo bhavet || 65 ||
65.d:
सर्वं जगत् स्वदेहं वा स्वानन्दभरितं स्मरेत् ।
युगपत् स्वामृतेनैव परानन्दमयो भवेत् ॥ 65 ॥
65.m:
One should recall the whole universe or one's own body as full of one's own bliss;
simultaneously, through one's own nectar, one becomes composed of supreme bliss. || 65

66.s:
kuhanena prayogeṇa sadya eva mṛgekṣaṇe |
samudeti mahānando yena tattvaṃ prakāśate || 66 ||
66.d:
कुहनेन प्रयोगेण सद्य एव मृगेक्षणे ।
समुदेति महानन्दो येन तत्त्वं प्रकाशते ॥ 66 ॥
66.m:
By the practice of magic, O gazelle-eyed one, right away
great bliss arises, through which reality shines forth. || 66

67.s:
sarvasrotonibandhena prāṇaśaktyordhvayā śanaiḥ |
pipīlasparśavelāyām prathate paramaṃ sukham || 67 ||
67.d:
सर्वस्रोतोनिबन्धेन प्राणशक्त्योर्ध्वया शनैः ।
पिपीलस्पर्शवेलायाम् प्रथते परमं सुखम् ॥ 67 ॥
67.m:
Through the blocking of all channels, as the breath-energy rises slowly,
at the moment of the ant-like creeping touch, supreme pleasure expands. || 67

68.s:
vahner viṣasya madhye tu cittaṃ sukhamayaṃ kṣipet |
kevalaṃ vāyupūrṇaṃ vā smarānandena yujyate || 68 ||
68.d:
वह्नेर् विषस्य मध्ये तु चित्तं सुखमयं क्षिपेत् ।
केवलं वायुपूर्णं वा स्मरानन्देन युज्यते ॥ 68 ॥
68.m:
One should cast the mind full of pleasure into the center of fire and poison;
or [leaving it] solitary, filled with breath, one becomes united with the bliss of love. || 68

69.s:
śaktisaṃgamasaṃkṣubdhaśaktyāveśāvasānikam |
yat sukham brahmatattvasya tat sukhaṃ svākyam ucyate || 69 ||
69.d:
शक्तिसंगमसंक्षुब्धशक्त्यावेशावसानिकम् ।
यत् सुखम् ब्रह्मतत्त्वस्य तत् सुखं स्वाक्यम् उच्यते ॥ 69 ॥
69.m:
The pleasure culminating in immersion into the energy agitated by union with the Śakti,
which belongs to the reality of the Absolute, that pleasure is called one's own. || 69

70.s:
lehanāmanthanākoṭaiḥ strīsukhasya bharāt smṛteḥ |
śaktyabhāve 'pi deveśi bhaved ānandasamplavaḥ || 70 ||
70.d:
लेहनामन्थनाकोटैः स्त्रीसुखस्य भरात् स्मृतेः ।
शक्त्यभावे ऽपि देवेशि भवेद् आनन्दसम्प्लवः ॥ 70 ॥
70.m:
Through the intensity of remembering the pleasure of woman by licking, churning, and embracing,
even in the absence of a consort, O Goddess of gods, an inundation of bliss occurs. || 70

71.s:
ānande mahati prāpte dṛṣṭe vā bāndhave cirāt |
ānandam udgataṃ dhyātvā tallayas tanmanā bhavet || 71 ||
71.d:
आनन्दे महति प्राप्ते दृष्टे वा बान्धवे चिरात् ।
आनन्दम् उद्गतं ध्यात्वा तल्लयस् तन्मना भवेत् ॥ 71 ॥
71.m:
When great bliss is attained, or when a relative is seen after a long time,
having meditated upon the arisen bliss, dissolved in it, one should make one's mind absorbed in it. || 71

72.s:
jagdhipānakṛtollāsarasānandavijṛmbhaṇāt |
bhāvayed bharitāvasthāṃ mahānandas tato bhavet || 72 ||
72.d:
जग्धिपानकृतोल्लासरसानन्दविजृम्भणात् ।
भावयेद् भरितावस्थां महानन्दस् ततो भवेत् ॥ 72 ॥
72.m:
From the expansion of the delight and relish caused by eating and drinking,
one should contemplate the state of plenitude; thence great bliss arises. || 72

73.m:
For the yogin whose self is single-minded in the unequaled happiness of tasting objects such as songs,
there is oneness with that, because the mind ascends through becoming absorbed in it. || 73

74.s:
yatra yatra manas tuṣṭir manas tatraiva dhārayet |
tatra tatra parānandasvārūpaṃ sampravartate || 74 ||
74.d:
यत्र यत्र मनस् तुष्टिर् मनस् तत्रैव धारयेत् ।
तत्र तत्र परानन्दस्वारूपं सम्प्रवर्तते ॥ 74 ॥
74.m:
Wherever the mind finds satisfaction, right there one should fix the mind;
in each such place, the intrinsic form of supreme bliss manifests. || 74

75.s:
anāgatāyāṃ nidrāyām praṇaṣṭe bāhyagocare |
sāvasthā manasā gamyā parā devī prakāśate || 75 ||
75.d:
अनागतायां निद्रायाम् प्रणष्टे बाह्यगोचरे ।
सावस्था मनसा गम्या परा देवी प्रकाशते ॥ 75 ॥
75.m:
When sleep has not yet arrived and the external realm has vanished,
that state is accessible to the mind; the Supreme Goddess shines forth. || 75

76.s:
tejasā sūryadīpāder ākāśe śabalīkṛte |
dṛṣṭir niveśyā tatraiva svātmarūpam prakāśate || 76 ||
76.d:
तेजसा सूर्यदीपादेर् आकाशे शबलीकृते ।
दृष्टिर् निवेश्या तत्रैव स्वात्मरूपम् प्रकाशते ॥ 76 ॥
76.m:
When the ether is variegated by the light of the sun, a lamp, or the like,
one's gaze should be fixed right there; the nature of one's own Self shines forth. || 76

77.s:
karaṅkiṇyā krodhanayā bhairavyā lelihānayā |
khecaryā dṛṣṭikāle ca parāvāptiḥ prakāśate || 77 ||
77.d:
करङ्किण्या क्रोधनया भैरव्या लेलिहानया ।
खेचर्या दृष्टिकाले च परावाप्तिः प्रकाशते ॥ 77 ॥
77.m:
With Karaṅkiṇī, Krodhanā, Bhairavī, Lelihānā,
and Khecarī, at the moment of the gaze, the supreme attainment shines forth. || 77

78.s:
mṛdvāsane sphijaikena hastapādau nirāśrayam |
nidhāya tatprasaṅgena parā pūrṇā matir bhavet || 78 ||
78.d:
मृद्वासने स्फिजैकेन हस्तपादौ निराश्रयम् ।
निधाय तत्प्रसङ्गेन परा पूर्णा मतिर् भवेत् ॥ 78 ॥
78.m:
Seated on a soft seat on one buttock, placing hands and feet without support,
through connection with that, the intellect becomes supreme and full. || 78

79.s:
upaviśyāsane samyag bāhū kṛtvārdhakuñcitau |
kakṣavyomni manaḥ kurvan śamam āyāti tallayāt || 79 ||
79.d:
उपविश्यासने सम्यग् बाहू कृत्वार्धकुञ्चितौ ।
कक्षव्योम्नि मनः कुर्वन् शमम् आयाति तल्लयात् ॥ 79 ॥
79.m:
Having sat down properly on a seat with arms half-bent,
fixing the mind on the space of the armpits, one attains peace through dissolution therein. || 79

80.s:
sthūlarūpasya bhāvasya stabdhāṃ dṛṣṭiṃ nipātya ca |
acireṇa nirādhāraṃ manaḥ kṛtvā śivaṃ vrajet || 80 ||
80.d:
स्थूलरूपस्य भावस्य स्तब्धां दृष्टिं निपात्य च ।
अचिरेण निराधारं मनः कृत्वा शिवं व्रजेत् ॥ 80 ॥
80.m:
Fixing an unblinking gaze upon an object of gross form,
and quickly making the mind supportless, one attains Śiva. || 80

81.s:
madhyajihve sphāritāsye madhye nikṣipya cetanām |
hoccāraṃ manasā kurvaṃs tataḥ śānte pralīyate || 81 ||
81.d:
मध्यजिह्वे स्फारितास्ये मध्ये निक्षिप्य चेतनाम् ।
होच्चारं मनसा कुर्वंस् ततः शान्ते प्रलीयते ॥ 81 ॥
81.m:
With the tongue in the center and the mouth wide open, placing awareness in the center,
and mentally uttering the sound 'ha', one dissolves then into the quiescent state. || 81

82.s:
āsane śayane sthitvā nirādhāraṃ vibhāvayan |
svadehaṃ manasi kṣiṇe kṣaṇāt kṣīṇāśayo bhavet || 82 ||
82.d:
आसने शयने स्थित्वा निराधारं विभावयन् ।
स्वदेहं मनसि क्षिणे क्षणात् क्षीणाशयो भवेत् ॥ 82 ॥
82.m:
Remaining on a seat or in bed, contemplating one's own body as supportless,
when the mind is diminished, one's mental dispositions dissolve in an instant. || 82

83.s:
calāsane sthitasyātha śanair vā dehacālanāt |
praśānte mānase bhāve devi divyaugham āpnuyāt || 83 ||
83.d:
चलासने स्थितस्याथ शनैर् वा देहचालनात् ।
प्रशान्ते मानसे भावे देवि दिव्यौघम् आप्नुयात् ॥ 83 ॥
83.m:
Or for one situated on a moving seat, through moving the body slowly,
when the mental state is completely calmed, O Goddess, one attains the divine current. || 83

84.s:
ākāśaṃ vimalam paśyan kṛtvā dṛṣṭiṃ nirantarām |
stabdhātmā tatkṣaṇād devi bhairavaṃ vapur āpnuyāt || 84 ||
84.d:
आकाशं विमलम् पश्यन् कृत्वा दृष्टिं निरन्तराम् ।
स्तब्धात्मा तत्क्षणाद् देवि भैरवं वपुर् आप्नुयात् ॥ 84 ॥
84.m:
Looking at the spotless sky, making one's gaze uninterrupted,
motionless in body, in an instant, O Goddess, one attains the form of Bhairava. || 84

85.s:
līnaṃ mūrdhni viyat sarvam bhairavatvena bhāvayet |
tat sarvam bhairavākāratejastattvaṃ samāviśet || 85 ||
85.d:
लीनं मूर्ध्नि वियत् सर्वम् भैरवत्वेन भावयेत् ।
तत् सर्वम् भैरवाकारतेजस्तत्त्वं समाविशेत् ॥ 85 ॥
85.m:
One should contemplate the entire ether as dissolved in the head, in the nature of Bhairava;
one enters into that all-embracing reality of splendor in the form of Bhairava. || 85

86.s:
kiñcij jñātaṃ dvaitadāyi bāhyālokas tamaḥ punaḥ |
viśvādi bhairavaṃ rūpaṃ jñātvānantaprakāśabhṛt || 86 ||
86.d:
किञ्चिज् ज्ञातं द्वैतदायि बाह्यालोकस् तमः पुनः ।
विश्वादि भैरवं रूपं ज्ञात्वानन्तप्रकाशभृत् ॥ 86 ॥
86.m:
A little is known, giving rise to duality; external light is once again darkness;
having known the universe and the rest to be the form of Bhairava, one bears infinite light. || 86

87.s:
evam eva durniśāyāṃ kṛṣṇapakṣāgame ciram |
taimiram bhāvayan rūpam bhairavaṃ rūpam eṣyati || 87 ||
87.d:
एवम् एव दुर्निशायां कृष्णपक्षागमे चिरम् ।
तैमिरम् भावयन् रूपम् भैरवं रूपम् एष्यति ॥ 87 ॥
87.m:
Just so in a dark night, when the dark fortnight arrives,
contemplating the dark form for a long time, one will attain the form of Bhairava. || 87

88.s:
evam eva nimīlyādau netre kṛṣṇābham agrataḥ |
prasārya bhairavaṃ rūpam bhāvayaṃs tanmayo bhavet || 88 ||
88.d:
एवम् एव निमील्यादौ नेत्रे कृष्णाभम् अग्रतः ।
प्रसार्य भैरवं रूपम् भावयंस् तन्मयो भवेत् ॥ 88 ॥
88.m: In the very same way, having first closed the eyes, spreading out before oneself / the dark-hued Bhairava form, contemplating it, one becomes absorbed in it. || 88

89.s:
yasya kasyendriyasyāpi vyāghātāc ca nirodhataḥ |
praviṣṭasyādvaye śūnye tatraivātmā prakāśate || 89 ||
89.d:
यस्य कस्येन्द्रियस्यापि व्याघाताच् च निरोधतः ।
प्रविष्टस्याद्वये शून्ये तत्रैवात्मा प्रकाशते ॥ 89 ॥
89.m: Through the obstruction and blocking of any sense organ whatsoever, / of [one who has] entered the non-dual void, right there the Self shines forth. || 89

90.s:
abindum avisargaṃ ca akāraṃ japato mahān |
udeti devi sahasā jñānaughaḥ parameśvaraḥ || 90 ||
90.d:
अबिन्दुम् अविसर्गं च अकारं जपतो महान् ।
उदेति देवि सहसा ज्ञानौघः परमेश्वरः ॥ 90 ॥
90.m: While reciting the syllable "a" without point of concentrated energy and without emission, O Goddess, / there suddenly arises the great torrent of knowledge, the Supreme Lord. || 90

91.s:
varṇasya savisargasya visargāntaṃ citiṃ kuru |
nirādhāreṇa cittena spṛśed brahma sanātanam || 91 ||
91.d:
वर्णस्य सविसर्गस्य विसर्गान्तं चितिं कुरु ।
निराधारेण चित्तेन स्पृशेद् ब्रह्म सनातनम् ॥ 91 ॥
91.m: Direct consciousness to the end of the emission of a letter accompanied by emission; / with a mind that is supportless, one touches the eternal Brahman. || 91

92.s:
vyomākāraṃ svam ātmānaṃ dhyāyed digbhir anāvṛtam |
nirāśrayā citiḥ śaktiḥ svarūpaṃ darśayet tadā || 92 ||
92.d:
व्योमाकारं स्वम् आत्मानं ध्यायेद् दिग्भिर् अनावृतम् ।
निराश्रया चितिः शक्तिः स्वरूपं दर्शयेत् तदा ॥ 92 ॥
92.m: One should meditate upon one's own Self as having the form of space, unconfined by the directions; / then Śakti, consciousness independent of support, reveals her essential nature. || 92

93.s:
kiṃcid aṅgaṃ vibhidyādau tīkṣṇasūcyādinā tataḥ |
tatraiva cetanāṃ yuktvā bhairave nirmalā gatiḥ || 93 ||
93.d:
किंचिद् अङ्गं विभिद्यादौ तीक्ष्णसूच्यादिना ततः ।
तत्रैव चेतनां युक्त्वा भैरवे निर्मला गतिः ॥ 93 ॥
93.m: Having first pierced some limb with a sharp needle or the like, and then / joining awareness right there, one attains pure movement in Bhairava. || 93

94.s:
cittādyantaḥkṛtir nāsti mamāntar bhāvayed iti |
vikalpānām abhāvena vikalpair ujjhito bhavet || 94 ||
94.d:
चित्ताद्यन्तःकृतिर् नास्ति ममान्तर् भावयेद् इति ।
विकल्पानाम् अभावेन विकल्पैर् उज्झितो भवेत् ॥ 94 ॥
94.m: "Within me, there is no inner organ such as the mind"—thus one should contemplate; / in the absence of conceptual constructions, one becomes free from conceptual constructions. || 94

95.s:
māyā vimohinī nāma kalāyāḥ kalanaṃ sthitam |
ityādidharmaṃ tattvānāṃ kalayan na pṛthag bhavet || 95 ||
95.d:
माया विमोहिनी नाम कलायाः कलनं स्थितम् ।
इत्यादिधर्मं तत्त्वानां कलयन् न पृथग् भवेत् ॥ 95 ॥
95.m: Māyā is the deluder by name; the function of limited agency (kalā) is impulsion; / contemplating thus the intrinsic nature of the realities, one is not separate [from the absolute]. || 95

96.s:
jhagitīcchāṃ samutpannām avalokya śamaṃ nayet |
yata eva samudbhūtā tatas tatraiva līyate || 96 ||
96.d:
झगितीच्छां समुत्पन्नाम् अवलोक्य शमं नयेत् ।
यत एव समुद्भूता ततस् तत्रैव लीयते ॥ 96 ॥
96.m: Observing a desire that has suddenly arisen, one should bring it to rest; / from wherever it arose, right there it dissolves. || 96

97.s:
yadā mamecchā notpannā jñānaṃ vā kas tadāsmi vai |
tattvato 'haṃ tathābhūtas tallīnas tanmanā bhavet || 97 ||
97.d:
यदा ममेच्छा नोत्पन्ना ज्ञानं वा कस् तदास्मि वै ।
तत्त्वतो ऽहं तथाभूतस् तल्लीनस् तन्मना भवेत् ॥ 97 ॥
97.m: “When desire has not arisen in me, or knowledge, who then indeed am I?” / In ultimate reality I am that [state]; dissolved in that, one should be intent on that.

98.s:
icchāyām athavā jñāne jāte cittaṃ niveśayet |
ātmabuddhyānanyacetās tatas tattvārthadarśanam || 98 ||
98.d:
इच्छायाम् अथवा ज्ञाने जाते चित्तं निवेशयेत् ।
आत्मबुद्ध्यानन्यचेतास् ततस् तत्त्वार्थदर्शनम् ॥ 98 ॥
98.m: When a desire or cognition has arisen, one should focus the mind [upon it], / single-minded with the thought that it is the Self; thence comes the vision of the ultimate truth. || 98

99.s:
nirnimittam bhavej jñānaṃ nirādhāram bhramātmakam |
tattvataḥ kasyacin naitad evambhāvī śivaḥ priye || 99 ||
99.d:
निर्निमित्तम् भवेज् ज्ञानं निराधारम् भ्रमात्मकम् ।
तत्त्वतः कस्यचिन् नैतद् एवम्भावी शिवः प्रिये ॥ 99 ॥
99.m: Cognition may be uncaused, supportless, and illusory; / in ultimate truth, it belongs to no one. One who contemplates thus becomes Śiva, O beloved. || 99

100.s:
ciddharmā sarvadeheṣu viśeṣo nāsti kutracit |
ataś ca tanmayaṃ sarvam bhāvayan bhavajij janaḥ || 100 ||
100.d:
चिद्धर्मा सर्वदेहेषु विशेषो नास्ति कुत्रचित् ।
अतश् च तन्मयं सर्वम् भावयन् भवजिज् जनः ॥ 100 ॥
100.m: Consciousness is the essential nature in all bodies; there is no distinction anywhere; / therefore, contemplating everything as consisting of that, a person conquers worldly existence. || 100

101.s:
kāmakrodhalobhamohamadamātsaryagocare |
buddhiṃ nistimitāṃ kṛtvā tat tattvam avaśiṣyate || 101 ||
101.d:
कामक्रोधलोभमोहमदमात्सर्यगोचरे ।
बुद्धिं निस्तिमितां कृत्वा तत् तत्त्वम् अवशिष्यते ॥ 101 ॥
101.m: When in the grasp of lust, anger, greed, delusion, pride, or envy, / having made the intellect motionless, that reality remains. || 101

102.s:
indrajālamayaṃ viśvaṃ vyastaṃ vā citrakarmavat |
bhramad vā dhyāyataḥ sarvam paśyataś ca sukhodgamaḥ || 102 ||
102.d:
इन्द्रजालमयं विश्वं व्यस्तं वा चित्रकर्मवत् ।
भ्रमद् वा ध्यायतः सर्वम् पश्यतश् च सुखोद्गमः ॥ 102 ॥
102.m: For one who meditates on and sees the universe as magical illusion, / or as diverse like a painting, or as whirling, there is the arising of joy. || 102

103.s:
na cittaṃ nikṣiped duḥkhe na sukhe vā parikṣipet |
bhairavi jñāyatāṃ madhye kiṃ tattvam avaśiṣyate || 103 ||
103.d:
न चित्तं निक्षिपेद् दुःखे न सुखे वा परिक्षिपेत् ।
भैरवि ज्ञायतां मध्ये किं तत्त्वम् अवशिष्यते ॥ 103 ॥
103.m: One should not cast the mind into pain, nor throw it into pleasure; / O Bhairavī, let it be known: what reality remains in the middle? || 103

104.s:
vihāya nijadehasthaṃ sarvatrāsmīti bhāvayan |
dṛḍhena manasā dṛṣṭyā nānyekṣiṇyā sukhī bhavet || 104 ||
104.d:
विहाय निजदेहस्थं सर्वत्रास्मीति भावयन् ।
दृढेन मनसा दृष्ट्या नान्येक्षिण्या सुखी भवेत् ॥ 104 ॥
104.m: Abandoning what resides in one's own body, contemplating "I am everywhere" / with a steady mind and a gaze seeing nothing else, one becomes joyful. || 104

105.s:
ghaṭādau yac ca vijñānam icchādyaṃ vā mamāntare |
naiva sarvagataṃ jātam bhāvayan iti sarvagaḥ || 105 ||
105.d:
घटादौ यच् च विज्ञानम् इच्छाद्यं वा ममान्तरे ।
नैव सर्वगतं जातम् भावयन् इति सर्वगः ॥ 105 ॥
105.m: "The cognition of a pot and so forth, or desire and such within me, / is it not all-pervading?"—contemplating thus, one becomes all-pervading. || 105

106.s:
grāhyagrāhakasaṃvittiḥ sāmānyā sarvadehinām |
yogināṃ tu viśeṣo 'sti sambandhe sāvadhānatā || 106 ||
106.d:
ग्राह्यग्राहकसंवित्तिः सामान्या सर्वदेहिनाम् ।
योगिनां तु विशेषो ऽस्ति सम्बन्धे सावधानता ॥ 106 ॥
106.m: Consciousness of the object of perception and the subject of perception is common to all embodied beings; / but for yogins there is a distinction: attentiveness to the connection [between them].

107.s:
svavad anyaśarīre 'pi saṃvittim anubhāvayet |
apekṣāṃ svaśarīrasya tyaktvā vyāpī dinair bhavet || 107 ||
107.d:
स्ववद् अन्यशरीरे ऽपि संवित्तिम् अनुभावयेत् ।
अपेक्षां स्वशरीरस्य त्यक्त्वा व्यापी दिनैर् भवेत् ॥ 107 ॥
107.m: Just as in one’s own, one should contemplate consciousness in another’s body as well; / abandoning regard for one's own body, one becomes all-pervasive within days.

108.s:
nirādhāraṃ manaḥ kṛtvā vikalpān na vikalpayet |
tadātmaparamātmatve bhairavo mṛgalocane || 108 ||
108.d:
निराधारं मनः कृत्वा विकल्पान् न विकल्पयेत् ।
तदात्मपरमात्मत्वे भैरवो मृगलोचने ॥ 108 ॥
108.m: Having made the mind supportless, one should not form conceptual constructions; / then, in the state where the self is the Supreme Self, one becomes Bhairava, O deer-eyed one. || 108

109.s:
sarvajñaḥ sarvakartā ca vyāpakaḥ parameśvaraḥ |
sa evāhaṃ śaivadharmā iti dārḍhyāc chivo bhavet || 109 ||
109.d:
सर्वज्ञः सर्वकर्ता च व्यापकः परमेश्वरः ।
स एवाहं शैवधर्मा इति दार्ढ्याच् छिवो भवेत् ॥ 109 ॥
109.m: The Supreme Lord is omniscient, omnipotent, and all-pervading; / "I am verily he, having the attributes of Śiva"—from this conviction, one becomes Śiva. || 109

110.s:
jalasyevormayo vahner jvālābhaṅgyaḥ prabhā raveḥ |
mamaiva bhairavasyaitā viśvabhaṅgyo vibheditāḥ || 110 ||
110.d:
जलस्येवोर्मयो वह्नेर् ज्वालाभङ्ग्यः प्रभा रवेः ।
ममैव भैरवस्यैता विश्वभङ्ग्यो विभेदिताः ॥ 110 ॥
110.m: Just as waves belong to water, flurries of flame to fire, and rays to the sun, / so these diverse movements of the universe belong to me alone, to Bhairava. || 110

111.s:
bhrāntvā bhrāntvā śarīreṇa tvaritam bhuvi pātanāt |
kṣobhaśaktivirāmeṇa parā saṃjāyate daśā || 111 ||
111.d:
भ्रान्त्वा भ्रान्त्वा शरीरेण त्वरितम् भुवि पातनात् ।
क्षोभशक्तिविरामेण परा संजायते दशा ॥ 111 ॥
111.m: By whirling and whirling with the body and swiftly falling onto the ground, / through the cessation of the energy of agitation, the Supreme state arises. || 111

112.s:
ādhāreṣv athavā 'śaktyā 'jñānāc cittalayena vā |
jātaśaktisamāveśakṣobhānte bhairavaṃ vapuḥ || 112 ||
112.d:
आधारेष्व् अथवा ऽशक्त्या ऽज्ञानाच् चित्तलयेन वा ।
जातशक्तिसमावेशक्षोभान्ते भैरवं वपुः ॥ 112 ॥
112.m: Either through inability [to grasp] objects of support, or through lack of knowledge, or through dissolution of the mind, / at the end of the agitation of the arisen mystic absorption of power, Bhairava's form [shines forth]. || 112

113.s:
sampradāyam imam devi śṛṇu samyag vadāmy aham |
kaivalyaṃ jāyate sadyo netrayoḥ stabdhamātrayoḥ || 113 ||
113.d:
सम्प्रदायम् इमम् देवि शृणु सम्यग् वदाम्य् अहम् ।
कैवल्यं जायते सद्यो नेत्रयोः स्तब्धमात्रयोः ॥ 113 ॥
113.m: Hear this tradition, O Goddess; I explain it completely: / isolation (kaivalya) arises instantly as soon as the eyes are made motionless. || 113

114.s:
saṃkocaṃ karṇayoḥ kṛtvā hy adhodvāre tathaiva ca |
anackam ahalaṃ dhyāyan viśed brahma sanātanam || 114 ||
114.d:
संकोचं कर्णयोः कृत्वा ह्य् अधोद्वारे तथैव च ।
अनच्कम् अहलं ध्यायन् विशेद् ब्रह्म सनातनम् ॥ 114 ॥
114.m: Having contracted both ears, and likewise the lower aperture, / meditating on [that which is] without vowel and without consonant, one enters the eternal Brahman. || 114

115.s:
kūpādike mahāgarte sthitvopari nirīkṣaṇāt |
avikalpamateḥ samyak sadyas cittalayaḥ sphuṭam || 115 ||
115.d:
कूपादिके महागर्ते स्थित्वोपरि निरीक्षणात् ।
अविकल्पमतेः सम्यक् सद्यस् चित्तलयः स्फुटम् ॥ 115 ॥
115.m: From standing over a great pit such as a well and gazing into it, / for one whose intellect is free from conceptual construction, the dissolution of the mind clearly occurs at once. || 115

116.s:
yatra yatra mano yāti bāhye vābhyantare 'pi vā |
tatra tatra śivāvāsthā vyāpakatvāt kva yāsyati || 116 ||
116.d:
यत्र यत्र मनो याति बाह्ये वाभ्यन्तरे ऽपि वा ।
तत्र तत्र शिवावास्था व्यापकत्वात् क्व यास्यति ॥ 116 ॥
116.m: Wherever the mind goes, whether externally or internally, / right there is the state of Śiva; because of its all-pervasiveness, where could it go? || 116

117.s:
yatra yatrākṣamārgeṇa caitanyaṃ vyajyate vibhoḥ |
tasya tanmātradharmitvāc cillayād bharitātmatā || 117 ||
117.d:
यत्र यत्राक्षमार्गेण चैतन्यं व्यज्यते विभोः ।
तस्य तन्मात्रधर्मित्वाच् चिल्लयाद् भरितात्मता ॥ 117 ॥
117.m: Wherever the consciousness of the All-Pervading Lord is revealed through the senses, / because of having the nature of its subtle elements, through the dissolution of consciousness, there is a state of plenitude. || 117

118.s:
kṣutādyante bhaye śoke gahvare vā raṇād drute |
kutūhalekṣudhādyante brahmasattāmayī daśā || 118 ||
118.d:
क्षुताद्यन्ते भये शोके गह्वरे वा रणाद् द्रुते ।
कुतूहलेक्षुधाद्यन्ते ब्रह्मसत्तामयी दशा ॥ 118 ॥
118.m: At the end of sneezing and so forth, in fear, in sorrow, in a chasm, or fleeing from battle, / at the moment of intense curiosity, at the end of hunger and so on, there is the state consisting in the reality of Brahman. || 118

119.s:
vastuṣu smaryamāṇeṣu dṛṣṭe deśe manas tyajet |
svaśarīraṃ nirādhāraṃ kṛtvā prasarati prabhuḥ || 119 ||
119.d:
वस्तुषु स्मर्यमाणेषु दृष्टे देशे मनस् त्यजेत् ।
स्वशरीरं निराधारं कृत्वा प्रसरति प्रभुः ॥ 119 ॥
119.m: When objects are being remembered, one should abandon the mind in the perceived location; / making one's own body supportless, the Master shines forth. || 119

120.s:
kvacid vastuni vinyasya śanair dṛṣṭiṃ nivartayet |
taj jñānaṃ cittasahitaṃ devi śūnyālāyo bhavet ||120 ||
120.d:
क्वचिद् वस्तुनि विन्यस्य शनैर् दृष्टिं निवर्तयेत् ।
तज् ज्ञानं चित्तसहितं देवि शून्यालायो भवेत् ॥120 ॥
120.m: Fixing the gaze on some object, one should withdraw it slowly; / that cognition along with the mind becomes a dwelling in the void, O Goddess. || 120

121.s:
bhaktyudrekād viraktasya yādṛśī jāyate matiḥ |
sā śaktiḥ śāṅkarī nityam bhavayet tāṃ tataḥ śivaḥ || 121 ||
121.d:
भक्त्युद्रेकाद् विरक्तस्य यादृशी जायते मतिः ।
सा शक्तिः शाङ्करी नित्यम् भवयेत् तां ततः शिवः ॥ 121 ॥
121.m: Whatever intellect arises in a dispassionate person from an excess of devotion, / that is the Śakti of Śaṅkara; one should constantly contemplate it; thence, one becomes Śiva. || 121

122.s:
vastvantare vedyamāne sarvavastuṣu śūnyatā |
tām eva manasā dhyātvā vidito 'pi praśāmyati || 122 ||
122.d:
वस्त्वन्तरे वेद्यमाने सर्ववस्तुषु शून्यता ।
ताम् एव मनसा ध्यात्वा विदितो ऽपि प्रशाम्यति ॥ 122 ॥
122.m: When another object is being perceived, there is voidness in all [other] objects; / meditating on that alone with the mind, even though known, it becomes pacified. || 122

123.s:
kiṃcijjñair yā smṛtā śuddhiḥ sā śuddhiḥ śambhudarśane |
na śucir hy aśucis tasmān nirvikalpaḥ sukhī bhavet || 123 ||
123.d:
किंचिज्ज्ञैर् या स्मृता शुद्धिः सा शुद्धिः शम्भुदर्शने ।
न शुचिर् ह्य् अशुचिस् तस्मान् निर्विकल्पः सुखी भवेत् ॥ 123 ॥
123.m: The purity which is remembered by people of limited knowledge is not purity in the doctrine of Śambhu; / for [there] nothing is pure nor impure; therefore, free from conceptual construction, one becomes happy. || 123

124.s:
sarvatra bhairavo bhāvaḥ sāmānyeṣv api gocaraḥ |
na ca tadvyatirekteṇa paro 'stīty advayā gatiḥ || 124 ||
124.d:
सर्वत्र भैरवो भावः सामान्येष्व् अपि गोचरः ।
न च तद्व्यतिरेक्तेण परो ऽस्तीत्य् अद्वया गतिः ॥ 124 ॥
124.m: The Bhairava reality is everywhere, accessible even in common things; / there is nothing beyond it—thus is the non-dual path. || 124

125.s:
samaḥ śatrau ca mitre ca samo mānāvamānayoḥ ||
brahmaṇaḥ paripūrṇatvāt iti jñātvā sukhī bhavet || 125 ||
125.d:
समः शत्रौ च मित्रे च समो मानावमानयोः ॥
ब्रह्मणः परिपूर्णत्वात् इति ज्ञात्वा सुखी भवेत् ॥ 125 ॥
125.m: Equal toward enemy and friend, equal in honor and dishonor; / knowing, “Because of the absolute plenitude of Brahman,” one becomes happy.

126.s:
na dveṣam bhāvayet kvāpi na rāgam bhāvayet kvacit |
rāgadveṣavinirmuktau madhye brahma prasarpati || 126 ||
126.d:
न द्वेषम् भावयेत् क्वापि न रागम् भावयेत् क्वचित् ।
रागद्वेषविनिर्मुक्तौ मध्ये ब्रह्म प्रसर्पति ॥ 126 ॥
126.m: One should never cultivate hatred anywhere, nor cultivate attachment at any time; / when freed from attachment and hatred, Brahman expands in the middle. || 126

127.s:
yad avedyaṃ yad agrāhyaṃ yac chūnyaṃ yad abhāvagam |
tat sarvam bhairavam bhāvyaṃ tadante bodhasambhavaḥ || 127 ||
127.d:
यद् अवेद्यं यद् अग्राह्यं यच् छून्यं यद् अभावगम् ।
तत् सर्वम् भैरवम् भाव्यं तदन्ते बोधसम्भवः ॥ 127 ॥
127.m: What is unknowable, what is ungraspable, what is void, what transcends non-existence— / all that is to be contemplated as Bhairava; at the end of that, awakening arises. || 127

128.s:
nitye nirāśraye śūnye vyāpake kalanojjhite |
bāhyākāśe manaḥ kṛtvā nirākāśaṃ samāviśet || 128 ||
128.d:
नित्ये निराश्रये शून्ये व्यापके कलनोज्झिते ।
बाह्याकाशे मनः कृत्वा निराकाशं समाविशेत् ॥ 128 ॥
128.m: Focusing the mind on external space—eternal, independent of support, void, / all-pervasive, and free from limitation—one enters the spaceless. || 128

129.s:
yatra yatra mano yāti tat tat tenaiva tatkṣaṇam |
parityajyānavasthityā nistaraṅgas tato bhavet || 129 ||
129.d:
यत्र यत्र मनो याति तत् तत् तेनैव तत्क्षणम् ।
परित्यज्यानवस्थित्या निस्तरङ्गस् ततो भवेत् ॥ 129 ॥
129.m: Wherever the mind goes, abandoning that very thing / instantly through non-abidance, one then becomes wave-free. || 129

130.s:
bhayā sarvaṃ ravayati sarvado vyāpako 'khile |
iti bhairavaśabdasya santatoccāraṇāc chivaḥ || 130 ||
130.d:
भया सर्वं रवयति सर्वदो व्यापको ऽखिले ।
इति भैरवशब्दस्य सन्ततोच्चारणाच् छिवः ॥ 130 ॥
130.m: "He who through terrifying sound makes all resound, who bestows all, who is all-pervading in everything"— / by continuously enunciating the word Bhairava in this manner, one becomes Śiva. || 130

131.s:
ahaṃ mamedam ityādi pratipattiprasaṅgataḥ |
nirādhāre mano yāti taddhyānapreraṇāc chamī || 131 ||
131.d:
अहं ममेदम् इत्यादि प्रतिपत्तिप्रसङ्गतः ।
निराधारे मनो याति तद्ध्यानप्रेरणाच् छमी ॥ 131 ॥
131.m:
From the occurrence of conceptions such as 'I' and 'this is mine',
the mind goes to the supportless; driven by meditation upon that, one attains peace. || 131

132.s:
nityo vibhur nirādhāro vyāpakaś cākhilādhipaḥ |
śabdān pratikṣaṇaṃ dhyāyan kṛtārtho 'rthānurūpataḥ || 132 ||
132.d:
नित्यो विभुर् निराधारो व्यापकश् चाखिलाधिपः ।
शब्दान् प्रतिक्षणं ध्यायन् कृतार्थो ऽर्थानुरूपतः ॥ 132 ॥
132.m:
'Eternal, omnipresent, supportless, all-pervading, and sovereign of all'—
meditating at every moment on these words, one accomplishes one's goal in accordance with their meaning. || 132

133.s:
atattvam indrajālābham idaṃ sarvam avasthitam |
kiṃ tattvam indrajālasya iti dārḍhyāc chamaṃ vrajet || 133 ||
133.d:
अतत्त्वम् इन्द्रजालाभम् इदं सर्वम् अवस्थितम् ।
किं तत्त्वम् इन्द्रजालस्य इति दार्ढ्याच् छमं व्रजेत् ॥ 133 ॥
133.m:
"All this exists devoid of reality, resembling an illusion;
what reality is there to an illusion?" From this conviction, one attains peace. || 133

134.s:
ātmano nirvikārasya kva jñānaṃ kva ca vā kriyā |
jñānāyattā bahirbhāvā ataḥ śūnyam idaṃ jagat || 134 ||
134.d:
आत्मनो निर्विकारस्य क्व ज्ञानं क्व च वा क्रिया ।
ज्ञानायत्ता बहिर्भावा अतः शून्यम् इदं जगत् ॥ 134 ॥
134.m:
"For the immutable self, where is knowledge, or where is action?
External entities are dependent on knowledge; therefore, this universe is void." || 134

135.s:
na me bandho na mokṣo me bhītasyaitā vibhīṣikāḥ |
pratibimbam idam buddher jaleṣv iva vivasvataḥ || 135 ||
135.d:
न मे बन्धो न मोक्षो मे भीतस्यैता विभीषिकाः ।
प्रतिबिम्बम् इदम् बुद्धेर् जलेष्व् इव विवस्वतः ॥ 135 ॥
135.m:
"Neither bondage is mine, nor is liberation mine; these are terrors for the frightened.
This is a reflection of the intellect, like that of the sun upon waters." || 135

136.s:
indriyadvārakaṃ sarvaṃ sukhaduḥkhādisaṃgamam |
itīndriyāṇi saṃtyajya svasthaḥ svātmani vartate || 136 ||
136.d:
इन्द्रियद्वारकं सर्वं सुखदुःखादिसंगमम् ।
इतीन्द्रियाणि संत्यज्य स्वस्थः स्वात्मनि वर्तते ॥ 136 ॥
136.m:
"All contact with pleasure, pain, and the like is mediated by the senses."
Having thus abandoned the senses, established in oneself, one abides in one's own self. || 136

137.s:
jñānaprakāśakaṃ sarvaṃ sarveṇātmā prakāśakaḥ |
ekam ekasvabhāvatvāt jñānaṃ jñeyaṃ vibhāvyate || 137 ||
137.d:
ज्ञानप्रकाशकं सर्वं सर्वेणात्मा प्रकाशकः ।
एकम् एकस्वभावत्वात् ज्ञानं ज्ञेयं विभाव्यते ॥ 137 ॥
137.m:
Knowledge illumines all; by all, the self is illumined.
Because of the single nature of each, knowledge and the known are contemplated as one. || 137

138.s:
mānasaṃ cetanā śaktir ātmā ceti catuṣṭayam |
yadā priye parikṣīṇaṃ tadā tad bhairavaṃ vapuḥ || 138 ||
138.d:
मानसं चेतना शक्तिर् आत्मा चेति चतुष्टयम् ।
यदा प्रिये परिक्षीणं तदा तद् भैरवं वपुः ॥ 138 ॥
138.m:
The mind, awareness, power, and the self: this tetrad,
when it is completely dissolved, O beloved, then that is the embodiment of Bhairava. || 138

139.s:
nistaraṅgopadeśānāṃ śatam uktaṃ samāsataḥ |
dvādaśābhyadhikaṃ devi yaj jñātvā jñānavij janaḥ || 139 ||
139.d:
निस्तरङ्गोपदेशानां शतम् उक्तं समासतः ।
द्वादशाभ्यधिकं देवि यज् ज्ञात्वा ज्ञानविज् जनः ॥ 139 ॥
139.m:
One hundred and twelve wave-free instructions have been stated in brief,
O Goddess, knowing which a person becomes a knower of wisdom. || 139

140.s:
atra caikatame yukto jāyate bhairavaḥ svayam |
vācā karoti karmāṇi śāpānugrahakārakaḥ || 140 ||
140.d:
अत्र चैकतमे युक्तो जायते भैरवः स्वयम् ।
वाचा करोति कर्माणि शापानुग्रहकारकः ॥ 140 ॥
140.m:
And united with any single one of these, he becomes Bhairava himself;
he performs actions through speech, conferring curses and grace. || 140

141.s:
ajarāmaratām eti so 'ṇimādiguṇānvitaḥ |
yoginīnām priyo devi sarvamelāpakādhipaḥ || 141 ||
141.d:
अजरामरताम् एति सो ऽणिमादिगुणान्वितः ।
योगिनीनाम् प्रियो देवि सर्वमेलापकाधिपः ॥ 141 ॥
141.m:
He attains freedom from old age and death, endowed with attributes such as atomicity;
he is beloved of the yoginīs, O Goddess, and master of every gathering. || 141

142.s:
jīvann api vimukto 'sau kurvann api na lipyate |
śrī devī uvāca |
idaṃ yadi vapur deva parāyāś ca maheśvara || 142 ||
142.d:
जीवन्न् अपि विमुक्तो ऽसौ कुर्वन्न् अपि न लिप्यते ।
श्री देवी उवाच ।
इदं यदि वपुर् देव परायाश् च महेश्वर ॥ 142 ॥
142.m:
Even while living, he is liberated; even while acting, he is not tainted.
The venerable Goddess said:
If this is the body of the Supreme [Goddess], O God, O Great Lord,

143.s:
evamuktavyavasthāyāṃ japyate ko japaś ca kaḥ |
dhyāyate ko mahānātha pūjyate kaś ca tṛpyati || 143 ||
143.d:
एवमुक्तव्यवस्थायां जप्यते को जपश् च कः ।
ध्यायते को महानाथ पूज्यते कश् च तृप्यति ॥ 143 ॥
143.m:
under this stated condition, who is muttered to, and what is recitation?
Who is meditated upon, O Great Master, who is worshipped, and who is satisfied? || 143

144.s:
hūyate kasya vā homo yāgaḥ kasya ca kiṃ katham |
śrī bhairava uvāca |
eṣātra prakriyā bāhyā sthūleṣv eva mṛgekṣaṇe || 144 ||
144.d:
हूयते कस्य वा होमो यागः कस्य च किं कथम् ।
श्री भैरव उवाच ।
एषात्र प्रक्रिया बाह्या स्थूलेष्व् एव मृगेक्षणे ॥ 144 ॥
144.m:
for whom is the fire oblation offered, and for whom is sacrifice performed, and what, and how?
The venerable Bhairava said:
This external ritual procedure here, O deer-eyed one, is only for gross minds.

145.s:
bhūyo bhūyaḥ pare bhāve bhāvanā bhāvyate hi yā |
japaḥ so 'tra svayaṃ nādo mantrātmā japya īdṛśaḥ || 145 ||
145.d:
भूयो भूयः परे भावे भावना भाव्यते हि या ।
जपः सो ऽत्र स्वयं नादो मन्त्रात्मा जप्य ईदृशः ॥ 145 ॥
145.m:
That contemplation which is repeatedly cultivated on the supreme state,
that is recitation here; subtle sonic resonance itself, the essence of mantra, is such an object of recitation. || 145

146.s:
dhyānaṃ hi niścalā buddhir nirākārā nirāśrayā |
na tu dhyānaṃ śarīrākṣimukhahastādikalpanā || 146 ||
146.d:
ध्यानं हि निश्चला बुद्धिर् निराकारा निराश्रया ।
न तु ध्यानं शरीराक्षिमुखहस्तादिकल्पना ॥ 146 ॥
146.m:
Meditation indeed is an unmoving intellect, formless and independent of support,
and meditation is not the imagining of a body, eyes, face, hands, and the like. || 146

147.s:
pūjā nāma na puṣpādyair yā matiḥ kriyate dṛḍhā |
nirvikalpe mahāvyomni sā pūjā hy ādarāl layaḥ || 147 ||
147.d:
पूजा नाम न पुष्पाद्यैर् या मतिः क्रियते दृढा ।
निर्विकल्पे महाव्योम्नि सा पूजा ह्य् आदराल् लयः ॥ 147 ॥
147.m:
Worship is not by means of flowers and the like; that firm thought which is formed
in the great ether free from conceptual construction—that absorption, through reverent devotion, is worship. || 147

148.s:
atraikatamayuktisthe yotpadyeta dinād dinam |
bharitākāratā sātra tṛptir atyantapūrṇatā || 148 ||
148.d:
अत्रैकतमयुक्तिस्थे योत्पद्येत दिनाद् दिनम् ।
भरिताकारता सात्र तृप्तिर् अत्यन्तपूर्णता ॥ 148 ॥
148.m:
For one established in any one of these contemplative devices, that nature full of plenitude
which arises day by day is satisfaction here, the ultimate plenitude. || 148

149.s:
mahāśūnyālaye vahnau bhūtākṣaviṣayādikam |
hūyate manasā sārdhaṃ sa homaś cetanāsrucā || 149 ||
149.d:
महाशून्यालये वह्नौ भूताक्षविषयादिकम् ।
हूयते मनसा सार्धं स होमश् चेतनास्रुचा ॥ 149 ॥
149.m:
In the fire that is the abode of the great void, the elements, senses, objects, and the like
are offered along with the mind; that is the oblation, with the ladle of awareness. || 149

150.s:
yāgo 'tra parameśāni tuṣṭir ānandalakṣaṇā |
kṣapaṇāt sarvapāpānāṃ trāṇāt sarvasya pārvati || 150 ||
150.d:
यागो ऽत्र परमेशानि तुष्टिर् आनन्दलक्षणा ।
क्षपणात् सर्वपापानां त्राणात् सर्वस्य पार्वति ॥ 150 ॥
150.m:
Sacrifice here, O Supreme Mistress, is contentment characterised by bliss.
Because of destroying all sins and protecting everything, O Pārvatī, || 150

151.s:
rudraśaktisamāveśas tat kṣetram bhāvanā parā |
anyathā tasya tattvasya kā pūjā kāś ca tṛpyati || 151 ||
151.d:
रुद्रशक्तिसमावेशस् तत् क्षेत्रम् भावना परा ।
अन्यथा तस्य तत्त्वस्य का पूजा काश् च तृप्यति ॥ 151 ॥
151.m:
the mystic absorption into the power of Rudra is that sacred field, the supreme contemplative realization;
otherwise, what worship would there be of that reality, and who would be satisfied? || 151

152.s:
svatantrānandacinmātrasāraḥ svātmā hi sarvataḥ |
āveśanaṃ tatsvarūpe svātmanaḥ snānam īritam || 152 ||
152.d:
स्वतन्त्रानन्दचिन्मात्रसारः स्वात्मा हि सर्वतः ।
आवेशनं तत्स्वरूपे स्वात्मनः स्नानम् ईरितम् ॥ 152 ॥
152.m:
One's own self is indeed everywhere the essence of pure consciousness and autonomous bliss;
immersion into its true nature is declared to be the bath of one's own self. || 152

153.s:
yair eva pūjyate dravyais tarpyate vā parāparaḥ |
yaś caiva pūjakaḥ sarvaḥ sa evaikaḥ kva pūjanam || 153 ||
153.d:
यैर् एव पूज्यते द्रव्यैस् तर्प्यते वा परापरः ।
यश् चैव पूजकः सर्वः स एवैकः क्व पूजनम् ॥ 153 ॥
153.m:
The very substances by which the Supreme-cum-Non-Supreme is worshipped or propitiated,
and whoever is the worshipper—that is all only that single One; where is worship? || 153

154.s:
vrajet prāṇo viśej jīva icchayā kuṭilākṛtiḥ |
dīrghātmā sā mahādevī parakṣetram parāparā || 154 ||
154.d:
व्रजेत् प्राणो विशेज् जीव इच्छया कुटिलाकृतिः ।
दीर्घात्मा सा महादेवी परक्षेत्रम् परापरा ॥ 154 ॥
154.m:
The exhalation goes out, the inhalation enters, curled in form by its own will;
that Great Goddess, extended in nature, the Supreme-cum-Non-Supreme, is the supreme sacred field. || 154

155.s:
asyām anucaran tiṣṭhan mahānandamaye 'dhvare |
tayā devyā samāviṣṭaḥ param bhairavam āpnuyāt || 155 ||
155.d:
अस्याम् अनुचरन् तिष्ठन् महानन्दमये ऽध्वरे ।
तया देव्या समाविष्टः परम् भैरवम् आप्नुयात् ॥ 155 ॥
155.m:
Abiding and coursing within Her in this sacrifice consisting of great bliss,
possessed by that Goddess, one attains the supreme Bhairava. || 155

156.s:
ṣaṭśatāni divā rātrau sahasrāṇyekaviṃśatiḥ |
japo devyāḥ samuddiṣṭaḥ sulabho durlabho jaḍaiḥ || 156 ||
156.d:
षट्शतानि दिवा रात्रौ सहस्राण्येकविंशतिः ।
जपो देव्याः समुद्दिष्टः सुलभो दुर्लभो जडैः ॥ 156 ॥
156.m:
Twenty-one thousand six hundred [breaths] by day and night
is taught as the recitation of the Goddess; it is easy to attain, [yet] difficult to attain by the dull-witted. || 156

157.s:
ity etat kathitaṃ devi paramāmṛtam uttamam |
etac ca naiva kasyāpi prakāśyaṃ tu kadācana || 157 ||
157.d:
इत्य् एतत् कथितं देवि परमामृतम् उत्तमम् ।
एतच् च नैव कस्यापि प्रकाश्यं तु कदाचन ॥ 157 ॥
157.m:
Thus this highest, supreme nectar has been declared, O Goddess;
and this should never be disclosed to anyone whatsoever: || 157

158.s:
paraśiṣye khale krūre abhakte gurupādayoḥ |
nirvikalpamatīnāṃ tu vīrāṇām unnatātmanām || 158 ||
158.d:
परशिष्ये खले क्रूरे अभक्ते गुरुपादयोः ।
निर्विकल्पमतीनां तु वीराणाम् उन्नतात्मनाम् ॥ 158 ॥
158.m:
to an outsider disciple, a rogue, a cruel person, or one undevoted to the guru's feet;
but to spiritual heroes whose intellects are free from conceptual construction, who are exalted souls, || 158

159.s:
bhaktānāṃ guruvargasya dātavyaṃ nirviśaṅkayā |
grāmo rājyam puraṃ deśaḥ putradārakuṭumbakam || 159 ||
159.d:
भक्तानां गुरुवर्गस्य दातव्यं निर्विशङ्कया ।
ग्रामो राज्यम् पुरं देशः पुत्रदारकुटुम्बकम् ॥ 159 ॥
159.m:
who are devoted to the circle of gurus, it must be given without hesitation.
Village, kingdom, city, country, sons, wife, family— || 159

160.s:
sarvam etat parityajya grāhyam etan mṛgekṣaṇe |
kim ebhir asthirair devi sthiram param idaṃ dhanam |
prāṇā api pradātavyā na deyaṃ paramāmṛtam || 160 ||
160.d:
सर्वम् एतत् परित्यज्य ग्राह्यम् एतन् मृगेक्षणे ।
किम् एभिर् अस्थिरैर् देवि स्थिरम् परम् इदं धनम् ।
प्राणा अपि प्रदातव्या न देयं परमामृतम् ॥ 160 ॥

161.s:
śrī devī uvāca |
devadeva māhadeva paritṛptāsmi śaṅkara |
rudrayāmalatantrasya sāram adyāvadhāritam || 161 ||
161.d:
श्री देवी उवाच ।
देवदेव माहदेव परितृप्तास्मि शङ्कर ।
रुद्रयामलतन्त्रस्य सारम् अद्यावधारितम् ॥ 161 ॥
161.m:
The venerable Goddess said:
O God of gods, O Great God, O Śaṅkara, I am completely satisfied! / Today the essence of the Rudrayāmala Tantra has been ascertained,

162.s:
sarvaśaktiprabhedānāṃ hṛdayaṃ jñātam adya ca |
ity uktvānanditā devi kaṇṭhe lagnā śivasya tu || 162 ||
162.d:
सर्वशक्तिप्रभेदानां हृदयं ज्ञातम् अद्य च ।
इत्य् उक्त्वानन्दिता देवि कण्ठे लग्ना शिवस्य तु ॥ 162 ॥
162.m:
and today the heart of all divisions of power is known.
Having spoken thus, the delighted Goddess embraced the neck of Śiva.
